messages:
maria: Heads-up — prod-dedicated canary rolled the new pos-enc kernel "fast-alibi" and we're seeing a tiny but nonzero NaN/token rate (~0.02%) on 8k+ sequence generation. Low volume but noticable regressions in customer A's long-context evals.

aj: Yikes. Any stack traces or signal patterns?

maria: Pasting the top of the stack + shortened logs:
```
RuntimeError: attention_kernel: NaN encountered in softmax accumulator
  at device kernels/attn/alibi_fast.cu:line 482
  aten::softmax -> aten::dropout -> attention_kernel
context: seq_len=8192, kv_len=8200, dtype=bf16, batch=1, model=hf/redwood-large
metrics: NaN_tokens=12, gen_tokens=54000, nan_rate=2.2e-4
```

maria: Canary config switch was: `posenc.default_kernel = "fast-alibi"` with compile flags `--use-bf16-kernels`.

aj: Does the NaN show up only with bf16? Any repro with fp32?

devon: I ran a quick repro harness locally w/ seq=8192 and couldn't hit NaN on fp32. Replicated on bf16 when accumulation path used v1 kernel. Suspect accumulation overflow or missing eps in softmax preconditioner.

kevin: Two things to consider: 1) ALiBi computes per-head slopes and multiplies by relative positions — those slopes can grow with large kv_len; 2) the fast kernel avoids per-token clamp for perf. Combined -> tiny exponent blowups.

devon: Agreed. Hypothesis: the fast-alibi path relies on fused exp + softmax using bf16 without fp32 accumulation, so intermediate exponentials exceed range for bfloat16 and produce inf/NaN that later cause NaN in softmax.

aj: If that's the case, we need a short-term mitigation plus a long-term API boundary. Short-term: revert canary to previous kernel or gate fast-alibi behind a feature flag that enforces fp32 accumulation for seq_len > X.

maria: We put a temporary feature-flag rollback for the affected tenants. But we need an actual fix for the kernel selection logic so this doesn't keep recurring.

kevin: Proposal for kernel-selection heuristic:
- If dtype==bf16 and (seq_len+kv_len) >= 4096 -> prefer fp32-accumulating kernel (slower but safe)
- If per-head slope max * kv_len > slope_threshold -> force clamp/eps in fused exp path
- Otherwise choose fast-alibi bf16 kernel.

devon: Implementation notes: add a posenc_adapter wrapper in runtime that computes a cheap worst-case bound: max_slope_est = max(head_slopes) * max_relative_pos. If bound > 1e3 (tunable) then pick safe kernel.

aj: That wrapper is the kind of interface boundary we want. Two questions: how expensive is computing head_slopes? It depends on model config but we can precompute per-model and stash in model-metadata.

kevin: Exactly. Store `posenc.metadata` with dtype-safety hints computed at model load time. Also expose `posenc.tolerance` per-deployment so customers can opt-in for performance vs risk.

maria: For the kernel change itself: devon, can you add a guarded clamp near the exponent compute path? e.g.
```c
// pseudo
float v = compute_slope_mul_pos(...);
if (v > V_CLAMP) v = clamp_to(v);
exp_accum += exp(v);
```
We want minimal branching to not kill perf on short sequences.

devon: I can add an approximate fast clamp (faster than branch): use `v = min(v, V_CLAMP)` via a vectorized instruction or `max`/`min` intrinsics on CUDA. Also add small eps inside softmax denom: `denom = max(sum_exp, 1e-6f)`.

aj: Add unit tests in eng-runtime/posenc/tests for: bf16 overflow scenarios, long kv lengths, and model-config slopes. Make them part of CI but marked flaky=false; we should be able to deterministically force the pathological slope for exact repro.

runtime-ci: Alert: added `eng-runtime.posenc.nan_regression` metric with 1m cadence. It will fire if NaN_rate > 1e-5 for any model for 3 consecutive windows.

kevin: Longer term: consider moving fused exp/softmax for ALiBi into a numerically robust primitive that takes an accumulation_dtype hint. That lets kernels be specialized at compile time for bf16-fast or bf16-safe (with fp32 accum).

maria: Tradeoffs: fp32-accum avoids NaNs but can double memory/regs and reduce throughput. We need an A/B experiment for short sequences to measure perf delta. If perf drop < 10% for 90% of workloads, we might default to safety for hosted customers.

devon: Action items:
- devon: implement fast clamp + eps guard in fast-alibi kernel, add nightly test to spike large slopes (ETA 2 days)
- aj: add posenc_adapter kernel-selection heuristic and model metadata path (ETA 3 days)
- kevin: add per-deployment tolerance flag and rollout plan (ETA 1 day)
- maria: coordinate rollback for affected tenants and own canary re-run when guards land (ETA today/ASAP)

aj: Also note we should add an API-level opt: `posenc.policy = ["performance","safe","auto"]` so customers can choose. `auto` is our heuristic.

maria: Sounds good. If devon can get a PR up tonight, I'll run canary tomorrow using the `auto` policy. :+1:

kevin: One extra note — KV-cache compaction code (eng-runtime caching) sometimes rewrites relative positions for prefix scans; ensure adapter uses the effective kv_len after compaction, not raw buffer size. I saw one repro where compaction made slope estimate wrong.

devon: Good catch. I'll read cache compaction hooks and add a test for effective_kv_len.

maria: Thanks all. We'll sync in the posenc followup meeting tomorrow and update the postmortem if we see more tenants impacted.

aj: Marking this thread for follow-ups. If you add PR links paste them here.

runtime-ci: note: rolling alert disabled for affected tenants after rollback.

maria: PRs: I'll paste once devon pushes.

(End of thread)
